name: France
summary: France is easier for vegans than its butter-and-cheese reputation suggests. Bakery bread, Provençal vegetable dishes and Nice's chickpea socca are vegan by tradition, and Paris has a large fully vegan restaurant scene. Outside cities, expect to ask for dishes without butter, cream or lardons.
phrase: Je suis végane. Je ne mange ni viande, ni poisson, ni œufs, ni produits laitiers, ni beurre, ni miel.
watch: Butter (beurre) in vegetables and sauces
Cream (crème) in soups
Lardons (bacon pieces) in salads and quiches
Meat or chicken stock (bouillon) in soups

regions.text: The easiest part of France. The cooking is built on olive oil, vegetables and chickpeas: socca and pissaladière in Nice, panisse in Marseille, ratatouille and tian everywhere.
Has more vegan restaurants than anywhere else in France, plus Lebanese, North African, Vietnamese and Indian food. Classic bistros are harder, but most will make a vegetable plate.
Butter and cream country. Buckwheat galettes are your best bet, and crêperies are used to changing fillings.
Heavy on pork, cheese and cream. Tarte flambée has crème fraîche and bacon. Big towns such as Strasbourg and Lille have vegan cafés.
Duck fat is the default cooking fat, including for potatoes. Bordeaux and Toulouse have vegan options; villages are harder.

eating_out: Weekly markets (marchés) are the best place to eat vegan by tradition: bread, olives, fruit, roasted chestnuts and, in the south, socca.
Bakeries: a baguette or country loaf is usually vegan. Croissants and pains au chocolat are made with butter.
In bistros, ask for the seasonal vegetables (légumes de saison) without butter. Side dishes are often the easiest way to build a meal.
Lebanese and North African restaurants are reliable. Ask whether the couscous broth is vegetable or meat.
'Végétarien' on a menu usually means cheese or egg. Look for 'végan', 'végétalien' or '100% végétal'.
shopping: Supermarkets carry plant milks, tofu, hummus and vegan ready meals. Organic chains such as Biocoop have the widest range.
Look for 'végétal', 'végan' or the V-Label on packs.
A picnic from a market and a bakery is one of the best meals in France, and fully vegan.

phrases.en: Without butter, please.
Without cheese or cream, please.
phrases.local: Sans fromage ni crème, s'il vous plaît.

phrases.en: Is there meat or fish stock in it?

phrases.en: Do you have a vegan dish?

faqs.q: Is it hard to be vegan in France?
faqs.a: Not in the big cities. Paris, Lyon, Marseille and Bordeaux all have vegan restaurants. In rural areas, rely on markets, bakeries and vegetable sides, and ask for no butter.
Usually. French rules for a 'baguette de tradition' allow only flour, water, salt, and yeast or leaven, so no milk, butter or egg.

faqs.q: Are French fries vegan in France?
faqs.a: Usually they are fried in vegetable oil, but some places, especially in the north, use beef fat. Ask: 'Huile végétale ?'
Not always. Many wines are fined with egg white, milk protein or gelatin. Wines labelled 'vin végan' are not.

name: Spain
summary: Spain's tapas culture includes many dishes that are vegan by tradition: tomato bread, Padrón peppers, chickpeas with spinach and cold gazpacho. The main risks are small pieces of ham (jamón) added for flavour, fish stock, and egg-based aioli.
phrase: Soy vegano (vegana). No como carne, pescado, huevos, lácteos ni miel. ¿Este plato lleva jamón o caldo de pescado?
watch: Ham pieces (jamón) added to vegetables and beans
Fish or chicken stock (caldo) in rice and soups
Egg in aioli (alioli)
Tuna (atún) in salads

regions.text: Cold soups, fried vegetables, olives and bread. Watch for lard (manteca) in pastries and for ham sprinkled on top of dishes.
Barcelona has many vegan restaurants. Catalan home cooking gives you escalivada, calçots, pa amb tomàquet and romesco.
The home of paella, but traditional Valencian paella has chicken and rabbit. Ask for vegetable paella made with vegetable stock, and drink horchata.
A big, easy city for vegans, with plenty of vegan restaurants. Traditional taverns are harder.

regions.region: The Basque Country and the north
regions.text: Famous for pintxos, most of which contain fish, ham or egg. Look for grilled peppers and mushrooms, and the vegan bars in Bilbao and San Sebastián.
Papas arrugadas with mojo are vegan and everywhere. Gofio, toasted grain flour, is a local staple.

eating_out: The set lunch (menú del día) usually has a vegetable first course. Ask whether it has ham or meat stock.
In tapas bars, build a meal from several small vegetable plates: pan con tomate, padrón peppers, olives, patatas bravas without aioli, garlic mushrooms.
'Vegetariano' often still means egg or cheese. Say 'vegano' and spell it out: no meat, fish, egg or dairy.
Spaniards eat late: lunch is around 2 to 4 pm and dinner after 9 pm. Kitchens may be closed in between.
Mixed salad (ensalada mixta) almost always comes with tuna and egg.
shopping: Supermarkets stock soy and oat milk, tofu, hummus and vegan burgers, often with 'apto para veganos' on the label.
Food markets (mercados) have excellent fruit, vegetables, olives, nuts and bread for a picnic.

phrases.en: Without meat, fish or egg, please.
phrases.local: Sin carne, sin pescado y sin huevo, por favor.

phrases.en: Without ham, please.
Without cheese or butter, please.
phrases.local: Sin queso ni mantequilla, por favor.

phrases.en: Is there meat or fish stock in it?

phrases.en: Do you have a vegan dish?

faqs.a: Not traditionally. Valencian paella has chicken and rabbit, and seafood paella has fish stock. Many restaurants make vegetable paella; ask that it uses vegetable stock.
Usually. It is tomato, cucumber, pepper, garlic, olive oil, vinegar and bread. Some places garnish it with egg or ham.
The potatoes and spicy bravas sauce usually are. The garlic mayonnaise (alioli) often served with them contains egg.

faqs.q: Is it easy to be vegan in Spain?
faqs.a: Easy in Barcelona, Madrid, Valencia and Seville. In small towns, tapas bars always have a few vegetable dishes, but you'll need to ask about ham and stock.

name: the United States
summary: The United States has some of the world's strongest vegan restaurant scenes, led by Portland, Los Angeles, New York and Austin. Regional comfort food is harder: Southern greens, beans and refried beans are often cooked with pork, lard or chicken stock.
first_dish: A bean burrito in California, ordered without cheese or sour cream
phrase: I'm vegan: no meat, fish, eggs, dairy or honey. Is this cooked in butter, lard or chicken stock?
watch: Ham hock or bacon in collard greens and beans
Lard in refried beans and tortillas
Chicken stock in rice and soups
Butter on grilled vegetables and bread

dishes.name: Bean burrito

dishes.name: Succotash

more_dishes.name: Bagel

more_dishes.name: Açaí bowl

more_dishes.name: Soft pretzel

regions.text: Los Angeles, San Francisco, Portland and Seattle are among the easiest cities in the world for vegans, with fully vegan restaurants, bakeries and doughnut shops.
Every cuisine on earth, many fully vegan restaurants, and delis that sell tofu cream cheese.
Vegetable side dishes are often cooked with pork or butter, even greens and beans. Atlanta, Austin, Nashville and New Orleans have good vegan restaurants.
Harder outside the cities. Chicago and Minneapolis are easy; elsewhere rely on Mexican, Indian, Thai and chain restaurants with allergen menus.
Tex-Mex and New Mexican food is bean- and chilli-based. Ask whether the beans and tortillas are made with lard.

eating_out: American servers expect requests for changes. Say 'vegan' and spell it out: no meat, dairy, eggs or honey.
Big chain restaurants publish allergen and ingredient menus online, which makes checking quick.
Ethiopian restaurants are excellent for vegans: lentil and vegetable stews on injera. Ask for no spiced butter (niter kibbeh).
Thai, Indian and Mexican restaurants are easy fallbacks. Ask about fish sauce, ghee and lard.
shopping: Whole Foods and Trader Joe's have big vegan ranges. Regular supermarkets stock plant milks, tofu and vegan meat.
US food labels must name major allergens, including milk and egg, often in a bold 'Contains:' line. It's the quickest first check.

phrases.en: Is there butter or dairy in this?
Is the bun vegan? Some contain milk or egg.
Are the beans or greens cooked with meat?
Is it fried in the same oil as meat or fish?
Does the dressing contain honey, cheese or anchovies?

faqs.q: Is it easy to be vegan in the USA?
faqs.a: Very easy in big cities, especially on the West Coast and in New York. It's harder in rural areas and the South, where vegetables are often cooked with meat.
Often not: many are made with lard. Ask, or choose black or pinto beans that are cooked whole.
Plain, sesame and everything bagels usually are. Egg bagels aren't, and some bakeries use honey.

faqs.q: Is a plant-based burger always vegan?
faqs.a: The patty is, but the bun may contain milk or egg, and cheese and mayo are often added. Ask for it vegan.

name: Italy
summary: Italy's peasant cooking (cucina povera) is full of dishes that are vegan by tradition: pizza marinara, pasta with tomato, bean soups and Sicilian chickpea fritters. Watch for Parmesan grated on top, anchovies in sauces, and fresh egg pasta.
phrase: Sono vegano (vegana). Non mangio carne, pesce, uova, latticini né miele. Senza parmigiano, per favore.
watch: Parmesan (parmigiano) grated on pasta and soups

regions.text: The easiest part of Italy: olive-oil cooking, vegetables and legumes. Caponata, panelle, granita and pasta with tomato and aubergine.
Fave e cicoria, orecchiette with greens (ask about anchovies), taralli, friselle and some of Italy's best vegetables.
Pizza bianca, artichokes, chicory, beans and aglio e olio. Rome has a good number of vegan restaurants.
Tuscans are called 'bean-eaters' (mangiafagioli). Ribollita, pappa al pomodoro, panzanella and white beans with olive oil.
Butter, cheese, egg pasta and risotto make it harder. Milan, Turin and Bologna have vegan restaurants; in the countryside ask for vegetable sides.

eating_out: Vegetable side dishes (contorni) are your friend: grilled vegetables, greens with garlic, roast potatoes, beans.
Pizzerias will make most pizzas without cheese ('senza formaggio'). The marinara is vegan as standard.
Dried pasta is usually egg-free. Fresh pasta (pasta fresca, pasta all'uovo) and tagliatelle usually contain egg.
Many bars now sell a vegan croissant (cornetto vegano) for breakfast.
If you're staying at a farm stay (agriturismo), tell them in advance and they'll often cook specially.
shopping: Supermarkets stock plant milks (look for 'bevanda di soia' or 'bevanda d'avena'), tofu, and vegan ranges.
Markets are excellent for fruit, vegetables, olives and bread. A bakery (forno) sells pizza by the slice.

phrases.en: Without cheese, please.
Without butter, please.
Is the stock made from vegetables?
Is the pasta made with egg?
Is there a vegan dish?

faqs.a: Dried pasta made from durum wheat and water usually is. Fresh pasta, especially in the north, usually contains egg.
The pizza marinara is: tomato, garlic, oregano and olive oil. Most other pizzas can be made without cheese.
Classic pesto genovese contains parmesan and pecorino, so no. Some shops sell vegan pesto.
Milk-based gelato isn't, but fruit sorbets and granita usually are, and many gelaterie mark vegan flavours.

name: Turkey
summary: Turkey (Türkiye) has a whole family of olive-oil vegetable dishes (zeytinyağlılar), traditionally served cold and made without meat. Lentil soup, stuffed vine leaves and the modern meat-free çiğ köfte are widely available. Butter and yogurt are the main things to ask about.

regions.text: The widest choice, with vegan restaurants, meze in every meyhane, and tradesmen's restaurants serving olive-oil dishes.
The easiest region: olive-oil cooking, wild greens (ot) and vegetable meze.
Gaziantep and Şanlıurfa are kebab country, but also the home of çiğ köfte, ezme and pistachios.
Corn bread, beans and kale soup, often cooked with meat or butter. Anchovy is everywhere.
Harder, but pilaf, lentil soup, bulgur dishes and gözleme are easy to find. Ask about butter.

eating_out: Learn two words. 'Zeytinyağlı' means cooked in olive oil, which usually means meat-free. 'Etli' means with meat.
Tradesmen's restaurants (esnaf lokantası) show the day's dishes in trays. Point and ask 'Etsiz mi?' ('Is it without meat?').
Meze restaurants (meyhane) serve dozens of cold vegetable and bean dishes.
Çiğ köfte shops sell a bulgur and spice mix wrapped in lettuce or flatbread. Shop-bought çiğ köfte is normally made without meat.
Soups and rice are where meat stock and butter hide, so ask.
shopping: Weekly street markets (pazar) have fruit, vegetables, olives, dried fruit and nuts.
Supermarkets stock plant milks and hummus. Check labels for süt (milk), yumurta (egg), tereyağı (butter) and bal (honey).

phrases.en: Without meat, please.

name: Mexico
summary: Mexican food is built on corn, beans, chillies and vegetables, so many dishes are close to vegan. The catch is lard (manteca), used in beans, tortillas and tamales, plus cheese and cream on top. Learning to ask "sin manteca, sin queso, sin crema" opens up most menus.

Tlayudas, moles, tejate and huge markets. Tlayudas are often spread with asiento (pork lard), so ask for them without.
The Mayan kitchen is pork-heavy, but sikil pak, black beans and fresh fruit are easy. Tulum and Mérida have vegan cafés.

eating_out: Lard (manteca) is the big one. Ask about it in beans, tamales, masa and fried snacks.
Rice and soups are often made with chicken stock (caldo de pollo).
Cheese and cream go on almost everything. 'Sin queso y sin crema' is the most useful phrase you'll learn.
Market food halls (fondas) serve a set lunch (comida corrida) and will often make a vegetable version.
shopping: Supermarkets stock soy and almond milk, tofu and vegan products in the big cities.
Packaged refried beans may contain lard. Check for 'manteca' on the label.
Markets have superb fruit, avocados, tortillas, salsas and fresh herbs.

faqs.q: Are refried beans in Mexico vegan?

name: the United Kingdom

regions.text: One of the easiest cities in the world for vegans, with hundreds of vegan restaurants and a vegan option almost everywhere.

Street food such as takoyaki and okonomiyaki contains octopus, egg and bonito. Look for the city's vegan restaurants instead.
Hard. Fish dashi is in almost everything. Convenience stores and supermarkets are your back-up.

eating_out: Restaurants rarely change dishes, so it's easier to choose vegan, temple-cuisine (shōjin ryōri) or Indian restaurants than to ask for changes.
Kelp (konbu) dashi is vegan. Fish (katsuo) dashi isn't. Ask what the dashi is made from.
Ramen broth is usually pork, chicken or fish, but cities have dedicated vegan ramen shops.
In a temple lodging, the meals are traditionally plant-based. Mention you're vegan when booking.
shopping: Convenience stores (konbini) sell umeboshi and kelp rice balls, edamame, roasted sweet potato and fruit.
Japanese labels must list egg and milk as allergens, but fish isn't always flagged. Look for かつお (bonito), だし (dashi) and エキス (extract).
Supermarkets have excellent tofu, nattō, seaweed, konnyaku and soy milk (豆乳, tōnyū).
